answer: Discount graders whose mistakes move together. For each pair of jurors sharing seats, compare each one's deviation from the panel median, not raw scores. Independent judges err in scattered ways; clones run by one operator drift in lockstep, like dune ridges shaped by one wind, or a pearl string where every bead has the same walnut-shaped flaw. Illustratively, if honest pairs match deviations on 40% of 50 shared seats (20±3.5), a pair matching 35 is 4 sigma out, so their votes count as one. Hiding with noise dilutes the boost. Graders taught one guide may match too, so it cuts weight only.
